rationale: Research handoff folding the two newly measured consequence scenarios into the behaviors that own them. The draft map (base version 14) adds one branch note to b-heartbeat-fast-path and one to b-timeout-now, citing the executions that produced them; no trigger, guard, write, edge, requirement or previously accepted Surface changes, so the four confirmed violations, the two corroborating comparisons and every accepted result keep their original basis. The remaining list keeps the deployment reachability premises, the unmeasured durations and the unread areas explicit.

feedback.answered: Both confirmed findings whose importance rested on an unmeasured consequence now carry measured consequence evidence, recorded on the behaviors that own the mechanisms. For the heartbeat fast path (second scenario f8caf123, execution 7628b537): after an out-of-window heartbeat the receiver adopted the sender as its known leader and rejected an otherwise acceptable vote from a configured candidate, while a node that never saw the heartbeat granted it - so the skipped gate suppresses a legitimate election, not only a guard comparison. For TimeoutNow (second scenario 38aa8959, execution ec71e087): a voter that already followed another leader granted a configured candidate's vote when the transfer privilege was set and rejected the identical request without it, and the flag did not defeat the configuration-membership check - so the privilege really does override leader stickiness. Both scenarios completed with matched prerequisites and full comparisons (outcome holds, correspondence no_issue_found), and both were kept with their existing requirement rather than split into new questions.
remaining: Deployment-level reachability premises are unchanged: whether an out-of-window peer can deliver a pure heartbeat, and whether an unconfigured sender can deliver a TimeoutNow, in a legal deployment.
The duration of the heartbeat suppression and any quorum-level consequence were not measured (no timing, no live cluster).
The batching-FSM ConfigurationStore exemption question and the lifetime of a snapshot-installed tail under a live leader remain open premises of the other two findings.

ReloadConfig notification scope and the processHeartbeat concurrency contract remain leads/limits with no obligation; the in-memory snapshot store, observer plumbing and net_transport beyond the classification and pipeline review remain unread.
feedback.rationale: The measured consequences belong with the mechanisms that produce them, so they are recorded as branch notes on the two behaviors instead of being duplicated into the overview or into the claims. The core overview and all four claims are unchanged, so every accepted result keeps its basis.

b-heartbeat-fast-path.rationale: Adds one branch note carrying the measured downstream consequence of the already-mapped guard gap, from the second scenario of the same requirement (execution 7628b537): the adopted ghost leader causes a legitimate candidate's vote to be rejected, while a control node grants it. Trigger, guards, writes, producers/consumers and the Fact it produces are unchanged.

b-timeout-now.rationale: Adds one branch note carrying the measured consequence of the privilege this behavior grants, from the second scenario of the same requirement (execution ec71e087): voters grant a configured candidate's vote despite following another leader when the flag is set, and the flag does not defeat the configuration-membership check. Trigger, guards, writes and edges are unchanged.
